title: Destructuring and spread
summary: Unpack values from arrays and objects, and copy or merge them with spread syntax.

quiz.explain: Array destructuring assigns by position: `a` gets 10 and `b` gets 20.

quiz.code:
const { name, age } = { name: 'Asha', age: 19 };
console.log(name);
quiz.explain: Object destructuring picks values by key name, not by position.

quiz.q: What does this program print? Write the array as it appears.
quiz.explain: `...a` spreads the items of `a` into the new array, followed by 3.

quiz.q:
What is the value of `copy.marks` and `original.marks` afterwards?

`const original = { marks: 50 };`
`const copy = { ...original, marks: 90 };`
quiz.explain: Spread makes a new object, so changing `copy` does not affect `original`. A property written after the spread overrides the copied one.

quiz.q: Complete the code to take `city` out of the object.
quiz.explain: Curly braces on the left side pull properties out of an object. Square brackets would unpack an array instead.

exercise.task:
In `unpack.js`, write and export four functions:

- `swap(pair)` takes `[a, b]` and returns `[b, a]` using array destructuring.
- `fullName({ first, last })` destructures an object **in the parameter list** and returns `'first last'`.
- `mergeLists(a, b)` returns a new array with the items of `a` followed by the items of `b` (use spread, do not change `a` or `b`).
- `withMarks(student, marks)` returns a **new** object with all fields of `student` plus `marks` (use spread, do not change `student`).
hints: Destructuring unpacks, spread copies. Neither of them changes the original data.
swap: `const [a, b] = pair;` then return `[b, a]`. fullName: `({ first, last }) => ...`. For the last two, put `...a` / `...student` inside the new array / object literal.
